text: This capstone closes with the checklist a real ServiceNow security architect actually keeps: six sections, one for every chapter of this course, each item specific and checkable against a real platform setting rather than a general impression.

Section one, role design: compare role count to headcount, flag near-identical role names as consolidation candidates, and confirm every custom role has a documented owner and reason. Section two, ACL patterns: confirm comparable sensitive fields use consistent controls, confirm which ACL level actually governs an extended table, and hunt for a leftover scripted answer equals true left over from testing. Section three, authentication: confirm the instance actually matches the organization's real SSO standard, confirm MFA is enforced somewhere in the path, and confirm exactly one monitored break-glass account exists.

Section four, data protection: know which sensitive fields rely on encryption versus ACLs alone, confirm non-production environments use masked data, and confirm export and attachment controls back up the field-level ACLs. Section five, security operations: confirm Security Incident Response and Vulnerability Response are actually configured, not just installed. Section six, governance: minimize who holds security_admin, enable the Audit flag on every sensitive field, and confirm retention actually satisfies the frameworks that apply.

Scoring Meridian honestly: before this capstone, it failed role design, ACL patterns, authentication, and governance. After Lesson 23's fixes, those sections pass for the specific items addressed — but data protection and security operations were never assessed at the same depth in these three lessons. Stating that limitation plainly matters: fixing three findings is not the same as completing a full review.

A passing score today is a snapshot, not a permanent state. Every one of Lesson 22's original findings existed precisely because nobody re-ran a check like this one for four years. A real architect runs the full checklist annually at minimum, and after any significant platform upgrade.

This checklist is also the real handoff ahead: every fix this capstone made now has to move safely from sub-production into Meridian's real production environment, and stay in sync as the platform evolves. That configuration-promotion problem is exactly where Course 11, ServiceNow DevOps, Testing & Deployment, picks up — closing the Enterprise Implementation stage and opening the next one.
